title: Subjunctive, να/ότι and negation
about: Greek has no infinitive: where English says "to go", Greek says *να πάω* with a personal ending. Verbs of wanting, being able, trying and asking take *να*; verbs of saying, thinking and knowing a fact take *ότι* or *πως*. The subjunctive and the imperative are negated with *μη(ν)*, the indicative with *δεν*. Conditions use *αν* without *θα*.

items.en: I want you to come with us.

errs.why: *θέλω* is followed by *να* + subjunctive: *θέλω να έρθεις*. *Ότι* reports a fact.

items.en: I think you're right.

errs.why: *νομίζω*, *λέω*, *ξέρω* (a fact), *πιστεύω* introduce a statement with *ότι* or *πως*.

items.en: I can swim very well.

errs.why: *μπορώ* always needs *να* before the next verb: *μπορώ να κολυμπάω*. Greek has no bare infinitive.

items.en: Don't be afraid! I'm here.

errs.why: A negative command uses *μη(ν)* + subjunctive: *μη φοβάσαι*, *μην ανησυχείς*. *Δεν* negates statements.

items.en: Let's go for a coffee.

errs.why: *ας* replaces *να*; you never use both: *ας πάμε*, *ας μείνουμε*.

parts: Ξέρω να μαγειρεύω, αλλά δεν ήξερα ότι ο Νίκος είναι σεφ.
items.en: I know how to cook, but I didn't know that Nikos is a chef.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ξέρω να* + verb means "know how to"; *ξέρω ότι* means "know that".

items.en: I don't want you to be late.

errs.why: After *να* the negation is *μη(ν)*: *να μην αργήσεις*.

items.en: If you come tomorrow, we'll go to the sea.

errs.why: In a condition about the future, *αν* takes the subjunctive without *θα*: *αν έρθεις*. *Θα* belongs in the main clause.

items.en: If I had money, I'd buy a house on Naxos.

errs.why: The conditional "would buy" is *θα* + imperfective past: *θα αγόραζα*. *Θα αγόρασα* expresses a guess about the past ("I must have bought").

items.en: I came to Greece to learn Greek.

errs.why: Purpose is *για να* + subjunctive: *για να μάθω*.

items.en: He left without saying anything.

errs.why: *χωρίς* before a verb needs *να*: *χωρίς να πει*.

items.en: The doctor told me not to eat salt.

errs.why: A reported order or advice uses *να* (negated *να μην*), not *ότι*: *μου είπε να μην τρώω*.

parts: Ελπίζω να μη βρέξει αύριο, γιατί θέλουμε να πάμε εκδρομή.
items.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow, because we want to go on a trip.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *ελπίζω να* + subjunctive, negated with *μη*; *θέλουμε να πάμε*.

items.en: Giannis said he would come tomorrow.

errs.why: A reported statement uses *ότι/πως* + the tense of the original (*θα έρθω* → *ότι θα έρθει*). *Είπε να έρθει* would mean "he said that someone should come".

parts: την αλήθεια, θα σου την έλεγα.
items.en: If I knew the truth, I would tell you.

errs.why: In unreal conditions *αν* takes the past without *θα*: *αν ήξερα*; *θα* goes in the main clause: *θα σου την έλεγα*.

items.en: I asked him to help me.

errs.why: *ζητάω* + an action takes *να*: *του ζήτησα να με βοηθήσει*.

items.en: It's important to read every day.

errs.why: Advice or necessity after *είναι σημαντικό/απαραίτητο/καλό* takes *να*. *Είναι σημαντικό ότι διαβάζεις* would mean "it matters that you (actually) read".

items.en: I don't know if she'll come to the party.

errs.why: An indirect yes/no question uses *αν* "whether". Here *αν θα* is correct, because this *αν* is not a condition.

parts: Δεν ξέρω αν θα προλάβω το τελευταίο τρένο.
items.en: I don't know whether I'll catch the last train.
items.why: Nothing to fix: in an indirect question ("whether") *αν* can be followed by *θα*. Only the conditional *αν* ("if") refuses *θα*.

items.en: I'm afraid we'll be late for the meeting.

errs.why: Fear that something may happen is *φοβάμαι μήπως* + subjunctive or *φοβάμαι ότι θα*. *Φοβάμαι να* means "I'm afraid to (do)": *φοβάμαι να οδηγήσω τη νύχτα*.

items.en: His mother insists that he study medicine.

errs.why: *επιμένω να* = insist on something being done; *επιμένω ότι* = insist that something is true (*επιμένει ότι είναι αθώος*).

items.en: If it hadn't rained, we would have left early.

errs.why: Past unreal condition: *αν* + pluperfect without *θα*, main clause *θα* + pluperfect.

items.en: If only I knew what she's thinking.

errs.why: *μακάρι* "if only" is followed by *να*: *μακάρι να ήξερα*, *μακάρι να έρθει*.

items.en: He acted as if he hadn't seen me.

errs.why: "As if" is *σαν να*, and after *να* the negation is *μη(ν)*: *σαν να μη με είδε*.

items.en: Having no other choice, she signed the contract.

errs.why: The gerund is negated with *μην* (or *μη*), never *δεν*: *μην έχοντας*, *μη γνωρίζοντας*.

parts: Αν δεν είχαμε επενδύσει τότε, σήμερα δεν θα υπήρχε η εταιρεία.
items.en: If we hadn't invested back then, the company would not exist today.
items.why: Nothing to fix: a mixed condition, past unreal *αν δεν είχαμε επενδύσει* with a present result *δεν θα υπήρχε*.
